status.en: 183 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 21% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 183 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 21 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to target security forces and civilians across northern Nigeria, killing police officers in Borno, Plateau, Sokoto-Gusau and ambushing a convoy in Zamfara. They abducted a Plateau university student, a husband and five others in Benue, 14 students in Niger, and mourners transporting a corpse to Benue, while also kidnapping worshippers and schoolchildren in Zamfara and Kaduna. Bandits killed five police officers heading to a Zamfara APC primary and killed a boxer in an Okada rider dispute in Ibadan. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpnede menn fortsetter å angripe sikkerhetsstyrker og sivile i Nord-Nigeria, og dreper politifolk i Borno, Plateau, Sokoto-Gusau og overfaller en konvoi i Zamfara. De bortførte en universitetsstudent fra Plateau, en ektemann og fem andre i Benue, 14 studenter i Niger og sørgende som fraktet en lik til Benue, samtidig som de kidnappet tilbedere og skolebarn i Zamfara og Kaduna. Banditter drepte fem politifolk på vei til en APC-primær i Zamfara og drepte en bokser i en tvist mellom en okada-fører og en annen i Ibadan. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
